selection.correct: 14B masked-stem correct; key is not the Algebra I primary modal letter and is not the lower-central numeric option.

correctExamples.originalStem: The cost of airing a commercial on television is modeled by the function C(n)  110n  900, where n is the number of times the commercial is aired. Based on this model, which statement is true?
correctExamples.maskedStem: The cost of airing a commercial on television is modeled by the function C(n)  [N]n  [N], where n is the number of times the commercial is aired. Based on this model, which statement is true?

options.A: The commercial costs $0 to produce and $110 per airing up to $900.
options.B: The commercial costs $110 to produce and $900 each time it is aired.
options.C: The commercial costs $900 to produce and $110 each time it is aired.
options.D: The commercial costs $1010 to produce and can air an unlimited number of times.

correctExamples.visibleCue: Numbers 110 and 900 remain in the options; the leftover C(n)=[N]n+[N] story maps the larger dollar amount to production and the smaller to per airing.

correctExamples.originalStem: Mike uses the equation b 5 1300(2.65)x to determine the growth of bacteria in a laboratory setting. The exponent represents
correctExamples.maskedStem: Mike uses the equation b [N] [N]([N])x to determine the growth of bacteria in a laboratory setting. The exponent represents

options.A: the total number of bacteria currently present
options.B: the percent at which the bacteria are growing

correctExamples.visibleCue: Growth model b=[N]([N])^x is still named; among verbal roles, the exponent is the number of time periods.

correctExamples.originalStem: The highest possible grade for a book report is 100. The teacher deducts 10 points for each day the report is late. Which kind of function describes this situation?
correctExamples.maskedStem: The highest possible grade for a book report is [N]. The teacher deducts [N] points for each day the report is late. Which kind of function describes this situation?
correctExamples.visibleCue: Highest grade with a constant deduction each late day is still a linear story after the 100 and 10 are hidden.

correctExamples.originalStem: The results of a linear regression are shown below. y  ax  b a  1.15785 b  139.3171772 r  0.896557832 r2  0.8038159461 Which phrase best describes the relationship between x and y?
correctExamples.maskedStem: The results of a linear regression are shown below. y  ax  b a  [N] b  [N] r  [N] r[N]  [N] Which phrase best describes the relationship between x and y?
correctExamples.visibleCue: The sign on r is still visible as a minus; the leftover asks for the relationship, so strong negative rather than positive or weak.

correctExamples.originalStem: If the zeros of the function g(x) are {3,0,4}, which function could represent g(x)?
correctExamples.maskedStem: If the zeros of the function g(x) are {[N],[N],[N]}, which function could represent g(x)?
correctExamples.visibleCue: The zero set is listed as three placeholders, so the matching polynomial is the three-factor option that includes an x.

correctExamples.originalStem: A cell phone company charges $60.00 a month for up to 1 gigabyte of data. The cost of additional data is $0.05 per megabyte. If d represents the number of additional megabytes used and c represents the total charges at the end of the month, which linear equation can be used to determine a user’s monthly bill?
correctExamples.maskedStem: A cell phone company charges $[N] a month for up to [N] gigabyte of data. The cost of additional data is $[N] per megabyte. If d represents the number of additional megabytes used and c represents the total charges at the end of the month, which linear equation can be used to determine a user’s monthly bill?
correctExamples.visibleCue: 60 and 0.05 are repeated in the option formulas; the leftover base-plus-per-megabyte story selects c=60+0.05d, not 60d.

wrongHighConfidenceExamples.originalStem: Sunny purchases a new car for $29,873. The car depreciates 20% annually. Which expression can be used to determine the value of the car after t years?
wrongHighConfidenceExamples.maskedStem: Sunny purchases a new car for $[N]. The car depreciates [N]% annually. Which expression can be used to determine the value of the car after t years?
wrongHighConfidenceExamples.visibleCue: Depreciation of [N]% per year; the model took (1+.20)^t (growth) over (1-.20)^t (decay) at margin 24.3.

wrongHighConfidenceExamples.originalStem: When solving the equation 4x2 2 16 5 0, Laura wrote 4x2 5 16 as her first step. Which property justifies Laura’s first step?
wrongHighConfidenceExamples.maskedStem: When solving the equation [N]x[N] [N] [N] [N] [N], Laura wrote [N]x[N] [N] [N] as her first step. Which property justifies Laura’s first step?

options.A: distributive property of multiplication over addition

wrongHighConfidenceExamples.visibleCue: Moving a term by adding to both sides; again assigned probability 1 to distributive property instead of addition property of equality.
